cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrians, beginning with “Share the roadway courteously and communicate location”.
cards.back: Share the roadway courteously and communicate location and intended movements to reduce crash risk.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrians, beginning with “Be ready to yield to pedestrians even outside”.
cards.back: Be ready to yield to pedestrians even outside crosswalks, and yield at intersection crossings even when unmarked.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrians, beginning with “Always yield to visually impaired people and stop completely”.
cards.back: Always yield to visually impaired people and stop completely for a crossing pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrians, beginning with “Yield to pedestrians already in an”.
cards.back: Yield to pedestrians already in an intersection even when your light is green.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrians, beginning with “A turn on red still”.
cards.back: A turn on red still requires readiness to yield to pedestrians.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrians, beginning with “Near parked or stopped vehicles, slow and do not”.
cards.back: Near parked or stopped vehicles, slow and do not pass until sure no pedestrian is crossing ahead of them.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrians, beginning with “Check for pedestrians before backing, particularly”.
cards.back: Check for pedestrians before backing, particularly in parking areas with many people.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrians, beginning with “In residential and playground areas, watch for children emerging”.
cards.back: In residential and playground areas, watch for children emerging between parked cars and be ready to stop, using a lower speed when appropriate.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrians, beginning with “In school zones, obey the lower speed when warning”.
cards.back: In school zones, obey the lower speed when warning lights flash or children are present, and stop or yield when crossing patrol signals it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “A bicycle on the roadway is a vehicle whose”.
cards.back: A bicycle on the roadway is a vehicle whose rider shares motorists’ rights, privileges, responsibilities and road rules.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Watch for cyclists because skill varies and an unpredictable”.
cards.back: Watch for cyclists because skill varies and an unpredictable rider may swerve, ignore controls or lack a night light.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Yield to bicyclists in intersections and where”.
cards.back: Yield to bicyclists in intersections and where a bike path or lane crosses a road.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Do not stop, park or drive in a designated”.
cards.back: Do not stop, park or drive in a designated bike lane or path except for alley or driveway access, official duties, police direction or an emergency.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Slow and give cyclists ample space, allowing a”.
cards.back: Slow and give cyclists ample space, allowing a cyclist to clear the intersection before you turn.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Avoid abrupt slowing or stopping in front of a”.
cards.back: Avoid abrupt slowing or stopping in front of a bicycle because a motor vehicle’s stronger brakes can create a collision risk.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Avoid sounding the horn close to a cyclist unless”.
cards.back: Avoid sounding the horn close to a cyclist unless needed to avert a crash, because startling the rider may cause a swerve.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Watch for cyclists entering the lane, especially”.
cards.back: Watch for cyclists entering the lane, especially children moving from a sidewalk into the road.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Do not turn sharply across a cyclist’s”.
cards.back: Do not turn sharply across a cyclist’s path or force the cyclist off the road.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Although cyclists must travel with traffic,”.
cards.back: Although cyclists must travel with traffic, look for riders anywhere on the roadway.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Use extra care around cyclists on wet, sandy or”.
cards.back: Use extra care around cyclists on wet, sandy or gravel-covered roads because those surfaces affect bicycles more strongly.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Cyclists signal turns and stops by hand, but conditions”.
cards.back: Cyclists signal turns and stops by hand, but conditions may require both hands on the bars, so also watch head or shoulder looks for intent.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Before opening a street-parked vehicle’s door,”.
cards.back: Before opening a street-parked vehicle’s door, check beside and behind for bicycles.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “Check for bicycles before backing,”.
cards.back: Check for bicycles before backing, particularly near schools and homes.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “For a same-direction bicycle pass at a posted limit”.
cards.back: For a same-direction bicycle pass at a posted limit of thirty-five miles per hour or less, allow at least three feet from the vehicle’s right side including projections to the bicycle’s left side.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “For that bicycle pass above a posted”.
cards.back: For that bicycle pass above a posted thirty-five-mile-per-hour limit, allow a minimum of six feet.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “A safe bicycle overtake may partly cross the centerline”.
cards.back: A safe bicycle overtake may partly cross the centerline or a same-direction lane line, and the required separation must last until safely past.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bicyclists, beginning with “The quoted Section thirty-two-twenty-six-twenty-six point one classifies”.
cards.back: The quoted Section thirty-two-twenty-six-twenty-six point one classifies a bicycle-passing violation as a Class two misdemeanor.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about motorcycles, beginning with “A motorcycle has the same road rights and responsibilities”.
cards.back: A motorcycle has the same road rights and responsibilities as another driver and must receive a full lane width rather than a shared lane.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about motorcycles, beginning with “Check mirrors and blind spots for hard-to-see motorcycles”.
cards.back: Check mirrors and blind spots for hard-to-see motorcycles and scan front and sides before a left turn.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about motorcycles, beginning with “Do not assume a flashing motorcycle signal means an”.
cards.back: Do not assume a flashing motorcycle signal means an imminent turn, because it may not cancel automatically; wait to confirm the rider’s action.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about motorcycles, beginning with “Follow a motorcycle by at least four”.
cards.back: Follow a motorcycle by at least four seconds and allow more time in wet conditions.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about motorcycles, beginning with “Expect a motorcycle to change lane position for potholes,”.
cards.back: Expect a motorcycle to change lane position for potholes, gravel, slippery patches, pavement seams, rail crossings or grooved pavement.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about motorcycles, beginning with “Scooters and mopeds usually”.
cards.back: Scooters and mopeds usually travel more slowly than motorcycles.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “The handbook reports more than two hundred fifty”.
cards.back: The handbook reports more than two hundred fifty thousand annual crashes between cars and commercial vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “Compared with cars, commercial vehicles generally maneuver less readily,”.
cards.back: Compared with cars, commercial vehicles generally maneuver less readily, have larger blind spots and need greater stopping, acceleration and turning room.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “The page’s loaded-truck example gives a stopping minimum of”.
cards.back: The page’s loaded-truck example gives a stopping minimum of two hundred ninety feet at fifty-five miles per hour on a clear, dry road with good tires and adjusted brakes.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “The handbook says a bus may need”.
cards.back: The handbook says a bus may need at least three hundred feet to stop.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “No Zones include both places a car disappears from”.
cards.back: No Zones include both places a car disappears from view and positions so close that a truck or bus cannot maneuver or stop safely.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “A large truck or bus has blind”.
cards.back: A large truck or bus has blind areas beside, behind and in front of it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “A truck’s right blind area begins behind the”.
cards.back: A truck’s right blind area begins behind the cab and may extend along the truck’s full length.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “If the commercial driver’s face is not visible in”.
cards.back: If the commercial driver’s face is not visible in the side mirror, avoid assuming the driver can see you.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “Stay beside a large vehicle only as long as”.
cards.back: Stay beside a large vehicle only as long as needed because a lane change or swerve can create a crash.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “This page’s loaded-truck example gives at least three hundred”.
cards.back: This page’s loaded-truck example gives at least three hundred thirty-five feet to stop from fifty-five miles per hour under ideal conditions with good tires and adjusted brakes.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “The same page describes the truck stopping example”.
cards.back: The same page describes the truck stopping example as more than one-and-a-half times a car’s stopping distance.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “Do not cut into a large vehicle’s stopping space,”.
cards.back: Do not cut into a large vehicle’s stopping space, and after passing wait until its whole front appears in the mirror before moving ahead and maintaining speed.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “A large vehicle’s rear blind area can extend up”.
cards.back: A large vehicle’s rear blind area can extend up to two hundred feet, so do not follow close enough to lose its driver’s view or your view ahead.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “Position a following vehicle where the truck”.
cards.back: Position a following vehicle where the truck driver can see it in the side mirrors.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “The handbook describes large vehicles using the right lane”.
cards.back: The handbook describes large vehicles using the right lane around thirty-five miles per hour on steep hills and advises avoiding that lane where possible on hills and near weigh-station reentry.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “Give a turning truck or bus room because it”.
cards.back: Give a turning truck or bus room because it may swing left or use another lane before completing a right turn.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “Do not move between a right-turning large vehicle”.
cards.back: Do not move between a right-turning large vehicle and the curb; wait until its turn is complete.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “When meeting an opposing truck, keep as far”.
cards.back: When meeting an opposing truck, keep as far right as possible to reduce sideswipe and wind-turbulence effects.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “If unsure about an oncoming truck or bus’s”.
cards.back: If unsure about an oncoming truck or bus’s speed, do not turn left in front of it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “Stop behind marked stop lines to preserve”.
cards.back: Stop behind marked stop lines to preserve the turning room they provide for large vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “Do not cut off a large vehicle to”.
cards.back: Do not cut off a large vehicle to reach an exit, turn or narrow construction lane.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “Merge with traffic speed and do not move in”.
cards.back: Merge with traffic speed and do not move in front of a truck or bus and then slow.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about large-vehicle space, beginning with “A truck or bus stopped on an acceleration lane”.
cards.back: A truck or bus stopped on an acceleration lane needs substantial distance to regain merging speed; steady traffic pace can help it enter without another stop.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bus, ramp and emergency vehicles, beginning with “Never park on a runaway truck ramp or its”.
cards.back: Never park on a runaway truck ramp or its entrance because a vehicle unable to brake may need it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bus, ramp and emergency vehicles, beginning with “Brake smoke can warn of a runaway truck or”.
cards.back: Brake smoke can warn of a runaway truck or bus, so move out of its path and do not enter ahead of it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bus, ramp and emergency vehicles, beginning with “In construction zones, signs and markings may be missing;”.
cards.back: In construction zones, signs and markings may be missing; do not pull ahead of a truck or bus and stop abruptly.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bus, ramp and emergency vehicles, beginning with “Watch ahead for a bus’s frequent stops and change”.
cards.back: Watch ahead for a bus’s frequent stops and change lanes before the stop if you need to avoid queuing behind it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bus, ramp and emergency vehicles, beginning with “Pass a parked bus cautiously because it may reenter”.
cards.back: Pass a parked bus cautiously because it may reenter traffic and pedestrians or children may run in front of it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bus, ramp and emergency vehicles, beginning with “An articulated bus has about three feet of tail”.
cards.back: An articulated bus has about three feet of tail swing, so leave enough room behind it for that movement.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bus, ramp and emergency vehicles, beginning with “Larger vehicles generally have greater blind spots, require more”.
cards.back: Larger vehicles generally have greater blind spots, require more maneuver and stopping space, and take longer to accelerate or pass.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bus, ramp and emergency vehicles, beginning with “Smaller vehicles are harder for”.
cards.back: Smaller vehicles are harder for truck and bus drivers to see.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about bus, ramp and emergency vehicles, beginning with “Yield to an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and”.
cards.back: Yield to an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and a siren by moving toward the road edge without blocking an intersection.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about enforcement stops, beginning with “During a police stop, move safely and promptly to”.
cards.back: During a police stop, move safely and promptly to the right outside the travel lane without obstructing other traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about enforcement stops, beginning with “Remain in the stopped vehicle”.
cards.back: Remain in the stopped vehicle unless the officer requests otherwise.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about enforcement stops, beginning with “For the stop described in the handbook, turn off”.
cards.back: For the stop described in the handbook, turn off the engine, activate hazard lights, use interior lights at night and lower the window to communicate.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about enforcement stops, beginning with “Stay calm with belts fastened, ask passengers to do”.
cards.back: Stay calm with belts fastened, ask passengers to do the same, keep hands on the wheel and minimize unnecessary movement.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about enforcement stops, beginning with “Provide license, insurance proof and registration when requested, first”.
cards.back: Provide license, insurance proof and registration when requested, first telling the officer where they are and reaching slowly with one hand kept on the wheel.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about enforcement stops, beginning with “Answer the officer clearly and”.
cards.back: Answer the officer clearly and fully and never flee law enforcement.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about slow and animal-drawn vehicles, beginning with “A rear fluorescent or reflective orange-and-red triangle on”.
cards.back: A rear fluorescent or reflective orange-and-red triangle on slow equipment indicates travel below twenty-five miles per hour.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about slow and animal-drawn vehicles, beginning with “Approach slow vehicles cautiously”.
cards.back: Approach slow vehicles cautiously and pass only when safe.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about slow and animal-drawn vehicles, beginning with “Watch rural roads for farm equipment crossing or traveling”.
cards.back: Watch rural roads for farm equipment crossing or traveling the highway, and do not assume its operator can hear an approaching car.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about slow and animal-drawn vehicles, beginning with “Animal-drawn vehicles and horseback riders have road-use rights”.
cards.back: Animal-drawn vehicles and horseback riders have road-use rights and must follow road rules, so pass carefully.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about slow and animal-drawn vehicles, beginning with “Do not sound the horn or rev the engine”.
cards.back: Do not sound the horn or rev the engine near horses because frightening them can cause a crash.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about slow and animal-drawn vehicles, beginning with “Expect animal-drawn vehicles to turn left into fields or”.
cards.back: Expect animal-drawn vehicles to turn left into fields or driveways and watch for posted warnings of these road users.
